learning_objective: 🎯 Understand the vital importance of water, the crisis of water scarcity in India, and the urgent need for conservation and watershed management!

main_concepts.simple_explanation: India has about 4% of the world's renewable water resources but 18% of its population. The distribution is highly uneven, leading to severe water stress in many regions.

Surface water includes rivers, lakes, and ponds (Ganga, Brahmaputra, and Indus basins hold the most). Groundwater is heavily utilized in states like Punjab and Haryana for irrigation, leading to dangerous depletion.
Agriculture is the biggest consumer of water in India (over 85%), primarily for irrigation. Industrial and domestic sectors consume less but are growing rapidly.
Industrial effluents, untreated sewage, and agricultural runoff (fertilizers) are severely degrading the quality of major rivers like the Ganga and Yamuna.
Sustainable solutions! Watershed management involves conserving water and soil within a catchment area. Rainwater harvesting captures rain directly for use or to recharge groundwater.

fun_activity.title: 🌧️ Be a Water Auditor
fun_activity.instructions: Track your household's water usage for a day. Notice how long the tap runs while brushing teeth or doing dishes. Find one way to 'harvest' or save at least 5 liters tomorrow!

exam_tips: 📌 Clearly explain the concept of 'Watershed Management' with examples like Haryali or Neeru-Meeru programs.
📌 Know the reasons for groundwater depletion in North-Western India (Green Revolution, water-intensive crops).
📌 Memorize the benefits of rainwater harvesting (reduces runoff, recharges aquifers, eco-friendly).
quick_recap: ⭐ The Ganga basin has the highest replenishable groundwater resources in India.
⭐ Arsenic and fluoride contamination in groundwater is a major health hazard in states like West Bengal and Rajasthan.
⭐ The National Water Policy prioritizes drinking water above all other uses.
